claim_verdicts.evidence: docker-compose.yml@stage-2 l.57-73: `db:` image postgres:17.6-alpine, container_name: donhang-db, ports "5432:5432". db/seed.sql header: "Fixed data for the lab: 8 products, 5 customers (one of whom never ordered), 12 orders." INSERTs: products ids 1-8, customers 1-5, orders 1-12.

dotnet.testcontainers.org (WebFetch): "Testcontainers for .NET is a library to support tests with throwaway instances of Docker containers"; it "requires a Docker-API compatible container runtime". Execution (lab up, unused by the test): docker events showed `container create name=romantic_tesla` then `container destroy name=romantic_tesla` 9 s later; PostgresFixture.DisposeAsync calls container.DisposeAsync().

PostgresFixture.cs@stage-2 l.14-17: `new PostgreSqlBuilder("postgres:17.6-alpine").WithDatabase("donhang").WithUsername("donhang").Build();` in a field initializer; l.28 `await container.StartAsync();` in InitializeAsync; l.33 `DisposeAsync() => await container.DisposeAsync()`. docker-compose.yml@stage-2 l.58 `image: postgres:17.6-alpine`; PostgresFixture.cs l.14 `new PostgreSqlBuilder("postgres:17.6-alpine")`. docker ps during the run listed the test container with image postgres:17.6-alpine.

Execution, lab's donhang-db on 5432 at the same time: `docker ps` -> `romantic_tesla|0.0.0.0:54753->5432/tcp` (session-1 run: 54407). Tests connect only via ConnectionString (no password in code), both pass, so the string carries host, mapped port, db and credentials.

docker-docs guides/postgresql.md: "When the container starts, it checks whether the PostgreSQL data directory is empty. If the directory already contains data, PostgreSQL starts immediately without running any initialization. If the directory is empty, the container runs `initdb` ... then executes all scripts in `/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/`". PostgresFixture.cs l.14-17: no mount/volume; round-1 run: only an anonymous volume, InitialCreate applied on it. version_key now docker, matching the source.

Opinion with stated reasons, supported: testing-with-the-database.md: "tests which modify data are more problematic, since they may interfere with one another"; "we must clean up the database between every test to avoid interference". Lesson states the cost (data others read, result depends on lab state), not an unconditional rule.

docker_system_events.yaml: "Use `docker events` to get real-time events from the server"; "Using the same filter multiple times is interpreted as a logical `OR`"; "Using multiple filters is interpreted as a logical `AND`"; filters `image=<repository or tag>`, `event=<event action>`; `destroy` listed. Execution printed exactly one create and one destroy line, kept streaming until killed.

Reviewer run 2026-10-01 on stage-2 extract (scratchpad it-a/s2), `dotnet test DonHang.Tests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~EfOrderRepositoryTests"`: "Passed!  - Failed: 0, Passed: 2, Skipped: 0, Total: 2". docker events (same filters): `container create name=romantic_tesla`, then `container destroy name=romantic_tesla`; no donhang-db line. Default output includes `name=` (docs example `(image=alpine:latest, name=test)`).

issues.text: Ambiguous pronoun makes a false reading available. The nearest antecedent of 'its' is EfOrderRepositoryTests, which has its own InitializeAsync (IAsyncLifetime, calls database.ResetAsync()) that xUnit runs before EACH test, not once per class (EfOrderRepositoryTests.cs l.14-19). Only PostgresFixture's InitializeAsync/DisposeAsync run once per class.
issues.quote: For `EfOrderRepositoryTests`, the test framework calls its `InitializeAsync` once before the first test of that class and its `DisposeAsync` once after the class's last test
issues.fix: Name the owner: 'For `EfOrderRepositoryTests`, the test framework calls `PostgresFixture`'s `InitializeAsync` once before the first test of that class and its `DisposeAsync` once after the class's last test; the next lesson shows how.'
